question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators="|"><mrow><mn>1,2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1,2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo></math> let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></math> be the number of subsets of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math>, each containing five elements out of which exactly <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> are odd. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>=</mo></math>

solution.text:
N1+N2+N3+N4+N5= Total ways – {when no odd}

Total ways =9C5

Number of ways when no odd, is zero     (∵ only available even are 2, 4, 6, 8)

∴ 9C5-zero=126
